problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $6a+\frac{b}{c}?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System (With Collinearity)

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $-2a+\frac{b}{c}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}30 & -60 \\ -60 & 120\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ -2 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

 Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
-2a+\frac{b}{c}=-2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\frac{2}{1}=3.
$$
